title: Oil a squeaky cabinet hinge with WD-40: a short burst into each gap between its knuckles, then work the door
instruction: The cabinet door's top hinge squeaks. Give each gap between its knuckles a short burst of WD-40 through the straw, swing the door open and shut three times to work it in, then stand the can on the table and leave the door shut.
context: Silencing a squeaky door with a can of WD-40 is one of the most familiar fixes in any home: spray the hinge through the straw, then open and close the door a few times to work the oil in, as WD-40's own guide says. Here the stream has to land in gaps 12.7 mm apart on a 9 mm barrel while the can's actuator pad is pressed (about 10 N), in short bursts rather than a flood.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the work surface and the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +305 and -305 mm. (1) Cabinet (fixed in place, as if screwed to the wall through its back; any small wall cupboard close to these sizes with an inset door on two 2-1/2 in butt hinges will do, or build it from these dimensions): a small wall cupboard of 18 mm pine with a 6 mm hardboard back, standing on the table, 306 mm wide (y -18 to +288 mm), 340 mm tall, 200 mm deep, its front face at x 460 mm. (2) Its door: inset, 266 x 300 x 18 mm pine, 0.62 kg, a 2 mm gap all round, shut. It hangs on its right-hand edge (the robot's right, at y 0) on two 2-1/2 in (63.5 mm) brass-plated steel butt hinges, each with five 12.7 mm knuckles on a 9 mm barrel and a loose pin with a button head; the barrels stand just proud of the face, their axis at x 455.5 mm, y +1 mm. The hinges' centres are 50 mm from the door's top and bottom edges: the top hinge (the squeaky one) is centred 270 mm above the table, so the four gaps between its knuckles are 251, 264, 276 and 289 mm above the table. A turned wooden knob, 28 mm across and 20 mm long on a 12 mm neck 12 mm long, is on the door's left-hand stile at y +233 mm, 170 mm above the table. (3) Can: an 8 oz WD-40 Multi-Use Product can with the Smart Straw, steel, 66.7 mm across and 171 mm tall to the top of its red actuator pad, 0.31 kg, standing upright on the table with its base centred at x 280, y -80 mm. A blue body with the yellow label panel, up to a silver domed top; on the dome sits the red actuator pad (about 64 mm long and 32 mm wide, flat on top over the valve, rounded at both ends, its front end overhanging the can), and a grey nozzle arm under the pad's front carries the red straw (3 mm across), flipped up into the stream position: it sticks out level, 105 mm beyond the nozzle, its tip 186 mm in front of the can's axis and 156 mm above its base, pointing straight away from the robot. The valve opens with the pad pressed about 1.5 mm (about 10 N in the simulation; measure the real can's opening force with a spring scale and note it). Nothing else is on the table. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the setup image.
scoring: Tools: a kitchen or jewellery scale reading to 0.1 g, the trial video, and a phone filming the top hinge in slow motion (60 fps, on a stand 15 cm to the right of the barrel, level with it, looking across it, its view checked in a dry run so the arms don't block it; a dark card behind the barrel so the stream shows; a strip of white masking tape on the cabinet's side board beside the barrel marked with each gap's height and lines 3 mm above and below it). Weigh the can just before and just after the trial: the difference is what was sprayed. A gap is oiled when the stream's first point of impact on the barrel (not splash) stays between that gap's two marks (within 3 mm of the joint line between two knuckles) for at least 6 frames of the 60 fps clip (0.1 s); a sweep up the barrel counts for each gap it holds on that long. A swing is the door opened past 45 deg and brought back to within 10 deg of shut; only swings after the fourth gap is oiled count. Score: 0 if the can lost more than 4 g (about 5 s of spraying: the hinge and cabinet flooded), whatever else holds. Otherwise 1.0 when all four gaps of the top hinge are oiled, the door is then swung at least three times, and at the end the door is within 5 deg of shut, the can stands upright on its base on the table (not leaning on the cabinet) and the robot is touching neither the can nor the door; 0.75 when all four gaps are oiled and the door is then swung at least once; 0.5 when all four gaps are oiled; 0.25 when at least two are; 0 otherwise.
reset_notes: Before the first trial, cover the gripper pads with replaceable tape, fit clear covers over the wrist cameras' lenses, and keep the close-up phone out of the stream's line. After each trial wipe the hinge, the door's edge, the cabinet's face and the pad covers with a paper towel; lay a fresh paper towel on the table under the hinge and tape kraft paper over the door and cabinet face round the hinge (cut away round the barrel) to catch overspray, changing them when wet. Oil left inside the hinge does not affect scoring (the squeak is not scored); every 20 trials, or once it drips, take the pin out, wipe it and the knuckles dry and refit it. Weigh the can and stand it back on its mark, straw flipped up and pointing away from the robot; shut the door. Replace the can when it sputters. Aerosol: ventilate, no flames.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The spray is a rule: with the actuator pad pressed 1.5 mm (a sprung valve, about 10 N) a straight stream leaves the straw's tip along it; where it meets the top hinge's barrel (within 3 mm of a gap) decides the gap, and spraying counts at 0.81 g/s. No liquid, drips or squeak are simulated; the door's friction stays the same. The straw is rigid in the stream position. The hinge leaves are hidden in the joint; the knuckles are drawn 0.5 mm apart.
